summary: Submitted draft/submission.json (action=check) with draft/check-plan-inactive.json and draft/check-harness-inactive.go, the first direct check for the accepted obligation c-client-request-completes-on-inactive-raft (unit unit-c-client-request-completes-on-inactive-raft). The check fixes one discriminator for the requirement: three nodes are created by the package's own NewRaft from the captured source and shut down through the public Shutdown(); because Shutdown().Error() calls waitShutdown, its return is the witness that the run, fsm and snapshot goroutines have exited, so no writer remains for any future. After that join the harness issues 128 VerifyLeader calls on a default-configured node (verifyCh has 64 slots) and 128 Apply calls on a node configured with the documented BatchApplyCh option (applyCh buffered), counts how many calls returned ErrRaftShutdown immediately versus returned a future, and after a bounded 250 ms wait inspects each returned future's own completion channel non-blockingly rather than calling Error(), which would block on exactly the futures under investigation. The asserted field is unresolved_total (eq 0), i.e. the direct count of client requests whose completion is still owed, with unresolved_verify, unresolved_apply and completed_shutdown_total reported beside it; a third default-configured node provides a diagnostic control in which the same select structure has an unbuffered channel (Barrier) and therefore completes every call, which separates the buffering from the API and from the shutdown state. I verified the exact submitted harness bytes locally in a fresh copy of the captured module: the test starts, exits 0, and emits unresolved_total = 128 (64 verify + 64 apply) with control_barrier_completed = 8 of 8, in three consecutive identical runs (earlier construction runs gave 64/64, 64/59 and 57/54 per path, so the schedule makes the per-path counts vary while the total stays far above zero). The plan records the fixed inputs, the binding bind-raft-verify-leader that locates the representative select, the oracle reasoning, the legality argument for permanence (the shutdown join, with the bounded wait explicitly demoted to corroboration), the schedule and configuration limits, and what remains outside the prefix (snapshot, bootstrap, configuration-change and restore channels are unbuffered; a request enqueued before shutdown rather than after it is not covered; only the VerifyLeader and batched-Apply instances are exercised). Optional preflight with the trusted validator returned valid=true; the target has not been executed for this product yet, so the next step would be the correspondence review of the resulting measured comparison.
